note: Part 10 (D = SCC-172). Two fail-opens in the main-write gate, both back-ported from AGY-59 where each was reproduced live. D3 is NOT swept here: it edits `.githooks/pre-push`, which `core.hooksPath` makes LIVE for this worktree's own pushes the moment it is saved (F22), so it lands last and is proven in a scratch repo instead - a sweep that leaves a mutated pre-push hook on disk between runs is not a risk worth taking for a third data point.

mutants.why: C1 - the hand-rolled --git-common-dir normalisation. git-for-windows answers `C:/...`, which does not match `/*`, so the repo root is prepended to an already-absolute path and the token is written nowhere: every push to main refused, on the PC only.
mutants.mutated: GIT_COMMON=$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null); case "$GIT_COMMON" in /*) : ;; *) GIT_COMMON="$REPO_ROOT/$GIT_COMMON" ;; esac

mutants.why: D1a - a push carrying no MERGE commit at all. Reproduced on AGY: a plain non-merge commit plus a token naming a never-existed branch came back APPROVED.

D1b - the token names a branch that does not resolve here. The original guard was `[ -n "$claimed" ] && [ "$merged" != "$claimed" ]`, so an EMPTY claimed skipped the comparison entirely and the gate approved a merge it could not identify.

D2 - the ZERO arm. Every check in this gate lived inside `remote_sha != ZERO` with no else, so a push CREATING main on a bare remote fell straight through to approved. AGY reproduced it with 3 stacked merges and 1 token.
mutants.original: refuse "this push would CREATE '$PROTECTED_REF' on the remote, which has no main yet.
mutants.mutated: : "this push would CREATE '$PROTECTED_REF' on the remote, which has no main yet.

mutants.why: the ZERO arm must refuse ON ITS OWN REASON. A shared banner would tell the operator to re-mint a token, which is not the problem and cannot fix it.
